title: 'nul character' generated by random() caused an error, once
description:
I used the following many times in an interactive session:

     random(8) |> rawToChar(multiple=F)

Once, the output was an error, due to a nul character. Below an extract of this session:

```
> random(8) |> rawToChar()
[1] "\\\xaf\024\xe9\xb2\017`\xb5"
> random(8) |> rawToChar(multiple=T)
[1] "\xa6" ">"    "\xf6" "\032" "Q"    "\xee" "9"    "\037"
> random(8) |> rawToChar(multiple=F)
Erreur dans rawToChar(random(8), multiple = F) : 
  caractère nul au milieu de la chaîne : '\020!\x9c\xac\x98\0\xccz'
> random(8) |> rawToChar()
[1] "\xe9_\xbc\xc73\x9d\xb7\x92"
> rawToChar('\020!\x9c\xac\x98\0\xccz')
Erreur : nul character not allowed (<input>:1:30)
> x <-'\020!\x9c\xac\x98\0\xccz'
Erreur : nul character not allowed (<input>:1:24)
```

"caractère nul au milieu de la chaîne" is French for "nul character in the middle of the string".

I then wondered whether random() was safe to generate, say, many salts, in a script. I launched the following several times (with or without print() ) and never got an error:

     for (i in 1:10000000) {random(8) }
     for (i in 1:10000000) {print(random(8)) }

I'm unsure whether this is relevant:
- I note that libsodium can generate the value 0 (https://doc.libsodium.org/generating_random_data)
- possibly related (?): https://github.com/jnr/jnr-ffi/issues/108

Using: sodium version 1.3.1
R version 4.5.0 (2025-04-11)
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS)
Session was running interactively in Konsole (KDE's shell terminal). The Linux shell says:

     $ echo $LANG
     fr_FR.UTF-8

Installation method that was used:
 
    $ sudo R
    > install.packages("sodium")

title: Expose XChaCha20 cipher
description:
libsodium supports the XChaCha20 cipher which has a 24-byte nonce.  This extended nonce makes nonce re-use a non-issue (if crypgraphically secure random bytes are used). 

See: https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/advanced/stream_ciphers/xchacha20

I'm happy to attempt a PR if this is considered worthwhile.

title: Question on Decrypting with sodium
description:
To communicate securely some information, I have:

 1. generated a public and private keys with the following command:
```
openssl req -x509 -nodes -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout <institution-retained>-private-key.pem -out <institution-provided>-public-key.pem
```

 2. shared the `public-key.pem` to a colleague that has used it to encrypt a string.

 3. I am now provided with this encrypted string of the form:

```
"-----BEGIN PKCS7-----\nMIIB7...OuVDPw==\n-----END PKCS7-----"
```

**Using `sodium::simple_decrypt`, how could I use my private key (in a `.pem` file) to decrypt this string?**
I have seen that in sodium vignette but I am not sure how I can adapt it:
```
library(sodium)
key <- keygen()
pub <- pubkey(key)
# Encrypt message with pubkey
msg <- serialize(iris, NULL)
ciphertext <- simple_encrypt(msg, pub)

# Decrypt message with private key
out <- simple_decrypt(ciphertext, key)
stopifnot(identical(out, msg))
```

PS: I have not encrypted the string and therefore don't know how to provide a reproducible example.

title: Efficiently decrypting vectors of GPS coordinates
description:
I am working with a fairly large dataset containing GPS coordinates encrypted with sodium in another programme. Now I need to decrypt them for analysis, but I am not sure how to do so efficiently. Please see the example below to see how I am currently decrypting data.

``` r
library(sodium)

# Create some fake GPS coordinates
data <- replicate(
  n = 400000,
  expr = paste0(
    sample(0:50, size = 1), ".", 
    paste0(sample(0:9, size = 14, replace = TRUE), collapse = "")
  )
)

# Generate keypair
key <- keygen()
pub <- pubkey(key)

# Encrypt message with pubkey
# Efficiency doesn't matter here
# For some reason, serialize doesn't work for my data
msg <- lapply(data, charToRaw) 
ciphertext <- lapply(msg, function(x) simple_encrypt(x, pub))
ciphertext <- lapply(ciphertext, bin2hex)

# Now for uncrypting
# How to do it faster?
out <- lapply(ciphertext, hex2bin)
out <- lapply(out, simple_decrypt, key = key)
out <- lapply(out, rawToChar)
out <- unlist(out)
identical(out, data)
#> [1] TRUE
```
<sup>Created on 2022-12-02 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

There are two components to this equation that slow down the process:
1. `sodium::hex2bin()` only accepts one value.
2. `sodium::simple decrypt()` only accepts one value.

Running `hex2bin()` on the encrypted data takes about 7 seconds on my machine, and decrypting takes 35 seconds. Please keep in mind that this is just an example; on real data, I would have to repeat this process many times. Normally, I would not know whether this is fast or slow (because I do not know much about encryption), but collapsing the `ciphertext` to a single string (using `paste()`) and then running `hex2bin()` provides a significant speed boost.

In an ideal world, you'd run vectorized functions:

```r
ciphertext |>
  hex2bin() |>
  simple_decrypt(key = key) |>
```

However, this is not possible with `sodium`.  Is there something wrong with my approach, or is this how one works with large vectors of data?

title: [Feature request] Clearer message when attr("nonce") is missing
description:
Hey, 

Thanks a lot for sodium :) 

I've been working on a tool that need to encrypt / decrypt data that are sent through http calls to a plumber API and stumble upon something that took me a little while to debug: when trying to decrypt a message, if you don't have `attr("nonce")`, the function will fail. 

```r
library(sodium)
key <- sha256(charToRaw("xyz"))
msg <- charToRaw("secretthing")

cipher <- data_encrypt(msg, key)
cipher
 [1] f6 d6 29 a5 5a c5 ed cd 31 6b cf 4b 19 19 3b 4f 56 9c b7 02 19 02 88 2c bd
[26] e2 14
attr(,"nonce")
 [1] 31 d6 f6 51 90 c7 6b 3a 70 e3 cc 14 94 c3 b5 a1 bf d9 d6 a8 87 0f 44 4e

# works as expected
data_decrypt(cipher, key) |> rawToChar()
[1] "secretthing"

# as I want to sent it via http, I use bin2hex
message_to_send <- bin2hex(cipher)
message_to_send
[1] "f6d629a55ac5edcd316bcf4b19193b4f569cb7021902882cbde214"

# on the other process, I receive a string that 
# I want to decrypt
message_received <- hex2bin(message_to_send)
message_received
 [1] f6 d6 29 a5 5a c5 ed cd 31 6b cf 4b 19 19 3b 4f 56 9c b7 02 19 02 88 2c bd
[26] e2 14

orig <- data_decrypt(message_received, key)
Error in data_decrypt(message_received, key) : 
  Invalid key. Key must be exactly 24 bytes
```

The error message here is pretty unclear because I haven't touched the `key` object and I don't understand why it's suddenly not the correct length, and so I spent some time trying to understand this `length` issue.

The issue here seem to be that the message_received doesn't have a `nonce` attribute : 

```r
attr(message_received, "nonce") <- attr(cipher, "nonce")
orig <- data_decrypt(message_received, key)
orig
 [1] 73 65 63 72 65 74 74 68 69 6e 67
```

Given that `nonce` in `data_decrypt` is `attr(bin, "nonce")` and that you can't encrypt with `NULL` (`data_encrypt(msg, key, NULL)` throws an error), my feature request would be that there should be a clear error message in `data_decrypt if` `nonce` is `NULL`.

Would it be an option to support Argon2 (https://download.libsodium.org/doc/password_hashing/the_argon2i_function) for password hashing as well? The problem is that it is only available from libsodium >= 1.0.9.

I would be happy to send a PR, if that is an option.

title: wouldn't data_tag() be more appropriate for authenticating _encrypted_ messages?
description:
hi jeroen, on sodium's [vignette]([https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sodium/vignettes/intro.html]) you talk about how data tagging can be used to authenticate a key,message pair, e.g.:

```{r}
key <- hash(charToRaw("This is a secret passphrase"))
msg <- serialize(iris, NULL)
mytag <- data_tag(msg, key)
```
however, since data is often times transmitted/stored in _encrypted_ format, i would think this function's more typical use would be to tag (msg_cipher,key) or even (msg_cipher,key_cipher) pair, e.g.:

```{r}
key <- hash(charToRaw("This is a secret passphrase"))
msg <- serialize(iris, NULL)
nonce <- random(24)
msg_cipher <- data_encrypt(msg, key, nonce)
mytag <- data_tag(msg_cipher, key) # or even my_tag <- data_tag(msg_cipher, key_cipher)
```
am i missing something?

title: hash() functions returns different values for OSX and Windows
description:
# Windows:
 sodium::hash(serialize("password",NULL))
 [1] 05 c7 52 fb 82 f7 8c 28 bb 28 e7 a6 16 aa 05 a2 cd 4a ea 39 61 48 ee f5 92 b7 3a b5 d2 2b 41 3b

# OSX
 sodium::hash(serialize("password",NULL))
 [1] 44 b7 84 6d e3 c3 09 b9 d1 0f aa 86 23 bf ea 28 b5 ac 6d 7e 9e c0 8a cf 4b c4 d3 b8 ac 46 ec 26

this is a problem since we would like to use an alphanumeric password and hash it
before calling the library. the above means that passwords wont work across platforms.

while serialize("password",NULL) has the exact same value on OSX and Windows (as it should):
> serialize("password",NULL)
 [1] 58 0a 00 00 00 02 00 03 04 01 00 02 03 00 00 00 00 10 00 00 00 01 00 04 00 09 00 00 00 08 70 61 73 73 77 6f 72 64

title: Method to encrypt a single field
description:
Often one needs to encrypt one or more fields  from a tibble/dataframe/data table with a function which returns the cypher to the appropriate row of the table, and then one would drop the plaintext. eg.

iris_confidential <- iris  %?>% mutate(
  encrypted_species = magic_function(species, ...)
 )  %>% select (-species)

I have been unable to coax sodium into doing a single-column encryption, or more precisely when I do I get an object back that has more observations than the data frame has rows.  One can't then push the resulting vector back into the data_frame.  If there a way to coax magic_function() out of sodium?

See:
```
```

> library(sodium)
> key <- hash(charToRaw("This is a secret passphrase"))
> msg <- serialize(iris$Species, NULL)
> str(msg)
 raw [1:748] 58 0a 00 00 ...
> nonce <- random(24)
> cipher <- data_encrypt(msg, key, nonce)
> 
> str(cipher)
 atomic [1:764] 55 31 fa 90 ...
 - attr(*, "nonce")= raw [1:24] 03 8e 9b 37 ...
```

```
You can't stuff either cipher or msg back into the data frame because the row-numbers don't align.
